synopsis: DEM, SPH or FEM terrain coupled with a multibody machine can predict granular flow, rutting and localized soil failure, but Chapter 8 describes this approach as high-fidelity, very slow and research-only for off-road validation [f6468, f6469, f6473]. Chapter 8 and the glossary recommend restricting these models to selected braking limit cases, including berms, deep aggregate and severe track-soil interaction; Chapter 11 additionally recommends high-detail simulation to understand stopping-distance sensitivity to soil, slope, payload and tire or track interaction [f6472, f13835, f8602]. This recommendation is constrained by the absence of evidence that such models are required for threshold prediction, their reported unsuitability for scenario sweeps and the risk that uncertain soil inputs overwhelm their fidelity [f6470, f6474, f6475]. Their computational burden calls for high-performance computing, with Chapter 11 identifying GPU acceleration and dedicated GPU or HPC workers as suitable [f6471, f8846]. Available tools include Project Chrono/Chrono::Vehicle with SCM, CRM and DEM terrain support, and Fraunhofer Demify for heavy-machinery soil DEM; Chapter 8 also reports that SCM's authors described SCM as “comparable” to DEM [f8494, f9123, f9141, f6463].
